title: ROI Cyber-Validator Data Validation Report
framing: This project has no historical incident data for the fictional company, so predictive accuracy cannot be measured. Following data-quality best practice (dimensions used by ISO/IEC 25012 and DAMA-DMBOK), we measure (1) how faithfully our data reproduces its official sources, (2) completeness, validity and consistency, (3) traceability of every number, (4) correctness and reproducibility of the calculation engine, and (5) how stable the recommendations are when assumptions change.

scorecard.metric: MITRE fidelity / CTID fidelity / published figures
mappings with evidence labels / inputs with source labels (backed by official sources; from published figures)
automated tests (pytest + vitest) / Python–TS parity / Monte Carlo range agreement
plan and Tool X finding unchanged under ±50% (one-at-a-time / joint)

mitre_fidelity.meaning: Each of the 28 ATT&CK techniques is checked against the official STIX for ID and URL, name, and mitigation / detection-strategy references (IDs, names, URLs) — 84/84 technique checks; every scenario step reference is checked for ID and name — 34/34 step checks. The file hash is checked against the provided original.
mitre_fidelity.evidence: MITRE Enterprise v19.2 STIX (enterprise-attack-19.2.json); compared against official STIX

ctid_fidelity.meaning: 179 of 179 Microsoft 365 mapping rows appear identically in the official CTID Mappings Explorer file (compared on 9 fields); the file hash is checked against the provided original.
ctid_fidelity.evidence: CTID Mappings Explorer M365 07/18/2025 (ATT&CK v16.1); compared against official CTID file

figures.name: FBI IC3 2025 — average loss per business email compromise complaint
figures.source_label: Average reported loss per business email compromise complaint, FBI IC3 2025: $3,046,598,558 ÷ 24,768 complaints = $123,005 (rounded).

figures.name: Sophos State of Ransomware 2026 — mean recovery cost excluding ransom
figures.source_label: Mean cost to recover from a ransomware attack, excluding any ransom paid: $1,700,200 (Sophos, The State of Ransomware 2026, n = 2,158).

published_figures.meaning: 2 of 2 published loss figures used by the model reproduce their cited values.
published_figures.evidence: risk_assumptions.json source labels; FBI IC3 2025 Internet Crime Report; Sophos State of Ransomware 2026

schema_validity.meaning: 7 of 7 data files validate against their strict Pydantic schemas.
schema_validity.evidence: Pydantic v2 validation of backend/data JSON files

referential_integrity.meaning: 100 of 100 cross-references (mapping techniques and tools, scenario assumptions, step and alternative techniques) resolve.

completeness.meaning: 49 of 49 scenario steps and techniques have their text, names and links.
completeness.evidence: step narrative and technique metadata checks

mapping_evidence_labels.meaning: 31 of 31 tool-to-technique mappings carry an evidence type and a visible evidence label.

mappings_backed_by_official_sources.meaning: 23 of 31 mappings (74.2%) are backed by MITRE or CTID; the rest are labelled as team assumptions or vendor descriptions.

python_ts_parity.meaning: 256 of 256 tool combinations give identical rounded ALE, risk score, severity and step outcomes in the Python and TypeScript engines.
python_ts_parity.evidence: Python engine vs frontend/scripts/engine-dump.mjs (TypeScript engine), all 2^n combinations

determinism.meaning: Repeated runs give identical point ALE and Monte Carlo percentiles (seed 42, 10,000 iterations).
determinism.evidence: double run of the baseline simulation

copy_compliance.meaning: 2 occurrence(s) of a banned phrase found in code or user-facing copy; see violations.
copy_compliance.evidence: scan of backend/app and frontend/src against 11 banned phrases

monte_carlo_agreement.meaning: Baseline P10 and P90 from the TypeScript engine are within ±3% of the Python engine (P10 0.51%, P90 0.32%). The two engines use different random number generators, so ranges are close but not identical.
monte_carlo_agreement.evidence: Python risk.run_monte_carlo vs frontend/scripts/engine-dump.mjs, baseline tools

one_at_a_time.meaning: Each of the 11 inputs is multiplied by 0.5 and 1.5 one at a time (probabilities capped at 1.0); plan unchanged in 22/22, Tool X low return in 22/22.

joint_perturbation.meaning: All 11 inputs multiplied together by Uniform(0.5, 1.5) (±50%), seed 7; plan unchanged in 500/500, Tool X low return in 500/500.

d5_decision_robustness.conclusion: Even if every assumption is off by up to ±50%, the recommended plan and the Tool X finding do not change in the tested runs.

limitations: No predictive validation is possible without real incident data for the fictional company.
CTID mappings use ATT&CK v16.1 while the scenarios use v19.2; 6 of 28 techniques have no CTID Microsoft 365 row (T1021.001, T1041, T1190, T1490, T1570, T1684.001).
Published loss figures are averages across organizations of all sizes; a few very large losses pull the mean up.
Tool costs and attack frequencies are sample assumptions (labelled in the app and editable in the Assumptions drawer).
